For the Strathbungo Film Society noir season, Thursdays in October and November 2024, back room of the Bungo Hall, 40 seats, £4 on the door. Screening licence through Filmbank, ref FB-58812. Ishbel picked half, I picked half, we argued about all of it.

## The rule

Classic period only, 1941 to 1958, Hollywood studio pictures. No neo-noir. Ishbel wanted "Chinatown" and lost. She'll get it at the next season.

## Screened

### 3 October: "Double Indemnity" (1944, Billy Wilder)

38 people. Barbara Stanwyck's anklet got a laugh, Fred MacMurray's "I killed him for money and for a woman" got silence. 107 minutes, the blinds-shadow lighting was the thing people talked about at the pub after.

### 10 October: "Out of the Past" (1947, Jacques Tourneur)

24 people, rain night. Robert Mitchum smoking for 97 minutes. Kirk Douglas is so smooth he's slimy. Flashback structure confused two people, see [[Screenwriting structure]] for why it works anyway.

### 17 October: "The Third Man" (1949, Carol Reed)

Full house, 40 plus six standing. Zither score by Anton Karas, Dutch angles everywhere, cuckoo clock speech. The Vienna sewers are real Vienna sewers. Somebody asked if we'd run a trip there, which is a no, but see [[Reise nach Wien]] if you're tempted.

### 31 October: skipped for Halloween

Horror night instead, see [[Horror movie night]].

### 7 November: "Sweet Smell of Success" (1957, Alexander Mackendrick)

Mackendrick grew up in Glasgow, so I did a five-minute intro on that. James Wong Howe shot it, Vaseline on the lenses for Burt Lancaster's glasses glare, apparently. 31 people.

### 14 November: "The Big Combo" (1955, Joseph H. Lewis)

The John Alton one. Single key lights, fog, figures as silhouettes. The final shot at the airfield is the best-lit thing in the season. Notes on Alton's book "Painting with Light" (1949) in [[Cinematography lighting]]. 19 people, the worst turnout, best film.

## Not screened, still want to

- "Detour" (1945, Edgar G. Ulmer), 68 minutes, shot in six days
- "Kiss Me Deadly" (1955, Robert Aldrich), the glowing briefcase
- "Touch of Evil" (1958, Orson Welles), the restored 1998 cut, for the opening tracking shot alone
- "Gun Crazy" (1950, Joseph H. Lewis again), the bank robbery done in one take from the back seat

## Totals

Five screenings, 158 tickets, £632 on the door. Licence fees £85 per title, so £425, plus £60 room hire. Profit £147, which went on the projector bulb. Next season pitch: Ealing comedies, spring 2025.
